nano17.name: ATI Nano17 force/torque sensor, SI-50-0.5 calibration
nano17.what_it_is: A tiny 6-axis force and torque sensor that feels the 0.3 mm cable press.

shape.note: 17 mm dia, 14.5 mm high, aluminium interface plates both ends

nano17.base_interface: 3 x M2x0.4 tapped 3.5 mm deep, equally spaced on 12.5 mm PCD; 2 x 2.0 mm slip-fit dowel holes 3.0 deep on 12.5 mm PCD (mounting side)
nano17.tool_interface: Same as base: 3 x M2x0.4 x 3.5 deep + 2 x 2.0 mm slip-fit dowel holes 3.0 deep on 12.5 mm PCD (tool side, dowel hole 2.035 to 2.060)
nano17.bolts: M2, max 3.5 mm engagement (damage if exceeded)
nano17.cable_power: Radial cable exit on mounting side ~48 deg from the +X axis; 5.3 mm cable, strain relief; connector is 17 mm dia x 67.5 mm long; goes to NetBox/DAQ (not the Meca tool port)
nano17.notes: SI-25-0.25 range: Fx,Fy 25 N, Fz 35 N, torque 0.25 Nm. Price on quote only. The owner brief names interface plates MC-OBB-1 etc; I could not find those names on any ATI page. The drawing says the plates are part of the sensor and must not be removed. Cable exit sits about 17.6 mm out from the axis on the drawing, so leave a notch. Calibration SI-50-0.5 chosen (Fxy 50 N, Fz 70 N, Txy and Tz 0.5 N m, resolution about 6 mN): the latch press acts 35 mm ahead of the flange axis, so a 10 N press is 0.35 N m of torque at the sensor, over the SI-25-0.25 range.

Max finger 20 g, finger reach sqrt(x2+z2)<=30 mm. Grip 40 N max, repeatability 0.03 mm. $1,675 at IP Tech Shop, $1,550 Tekmatic, $1,995 Applied (older snapshots, UNVERIFIED today). smc_lehz10.base_interface: Body only, no end-face mount: from the two side faces (mounting reference plane): 2 x M3x0.5x6 deep + 2 x O2.5H9 pin holes 2.5 deep on one side; 2 x M4x0.7x6 deep tapped with 2 x O3.3 through on the other (positions along the axis read off the drawing: 12 and 17 mm, ESTIMATE); also 2 x O5 on the connector side
smc_lehz10.tool_interface: Standard jaws (finger option Nil): jaw plate 12 wide x 5 thick (0/-0.05), 4 x M2.5x0.45 tapped in the open/close direction, hole centres 3 and 5.7 mm from the jaw tip (2 per jaw, ESTIMATE on layout); closed gap 11 mm, open 15 mm (stroke 4 total = 2 per jaw). Option A side-tapped M2.5 (A=3, B=5.7, C=2); option B through O2.9; option C flat fingers with 2H9 pin + M2.5 x 5 deep
smc_lehz10.cable_power: 24 V DC +/-10% from the controller; compact LEHZ10/16: 8 W operating, 7 W standby, 14 W peak incl. controller = ~0.6 A peak (0.33 A running); motor cable ~300 mm, robotic cable R1/R3/R5 option
smc_lehz10.notes: Force: compact 2 to 6 N (basic LEHZ10K2-4: 6 to 14 N), set as pushing force 40 to 100 percent in step data, only at pushing speed 5 to 20 mm/s; accuracy +/-30 percent of full scale (about +/-1.8 N). Stroke 4 mm both sides = 2 mm per jaw. Max 6 N: CANNOT reach 8 N; use LEHZ16LK2-6 (3 to 8 N, 3 mm per jaw, 190 g, jaw block 35 x 23.7, L 96.2, jaw 8 thick, 4 x M3x0.5) for the 3 to 8 N brief. Speed 5 to 80 mm/s open/close, 5 to 50 push; repeatability +/-0.02 mm; backlash 0.25. Price: 605 is the K2-4 basic listing (SmcPneumatics); compact LEHZ16LK2-6-R3 listed 800 at PMI; controller JXC51/61 ~257, JXC91 ~515 (different-model listings, ESTIMATE). Note EtherNet/IP is JXC91, not JXCE1 (EtherCAT). Buy: SMC USA (smcusa.com) or a local SMC distributor by part number; the online reseller page blocks robots, so the catalogue PDF is linked.

dh_pge_8_14.name: DH Robotics PGE-8-14 slim electric parallel gripper (alternative)

shape.note: 97 x 62 x 31 per DH listing; axis assignment ESTIMATE

dh_pge_8_14.base_interface: Mounting holes not read (DH drawing only; M3 pattern ESTIMATE)

smc_lehz16l.name: SMC LEHZ16LK2-6 electric parallel gripper (compact motor), with JXC51/61 (parallel IO) or JXC91 (EtherNet/IP) controller
smc_lehz16l.part_number: LEHZ16LK2-6 (+ JXC51 or JXC61, or JXC91)
smc_lehz16l.what_it_is: Compact electric 2-finger gripper, 3 mm stroke per jaw, gripping force settable 3 to 8 N (pushing force 40 to 100 percent in the step data), open-loop force (+-30 percent): the LR Mate's gripper, chosen because it can pinch the cable gently.

shape.note: 96.2 motor top to body bottom x 35 x 23.7 (width and depth read off the catalogue drawing: ESTIMATE); standard jaws project about 40 mm more

smc_lehz16l.base_interface: Side faces: 2 x M3 + 2 x 2.5 H9 pins on one face, 2 x M4 tapped / 3.3 through on the other (no end-face mount)
smc_lehz16l.tool_interface: Jaws on the end face: 4 x M3x0.5 tapped per jaw on a 14 x 8 mm plate, in the open/close direction (layout partly ESTIMATE)
smc_lehz16l.cable_power: 24 V DC +/-10% from the controller; compact LEHZ10/16: 8 W operating, 7 W standby, 14 W peak incl. controller = ~0.6 A peak (0.33 A running); motor cable ~300 mm, robotic cable R1/R3/R5 option
smc_lehz16l.notes: 3 to 8 N; 40 percent force only at pushing speed 5 to 20 mm/s; accuracy +-30 percent of full scale (about +-2.4 N), so bench-calibrate the force with a scale. About $800 for the gripper, controllers $257 to $515 (ESTIMATE). EtherNet/IP is the JXC91; JXCE1 is EtherCAT; parallel IO JXC51 (NPN) or JXC61 (PNP): confirm the FANUC DO polarity. Buy: SMC USA (smcusa.com) or a local SMC distributor by part number; the online reseller page blocks robots, so the catalogue PDF is linked.

nano25.name: ATI Nano25 force/torque sensor, SI-125-3 calibration
nano25.what_it_is: The six-axis force and torque sensor between the flange and the gripper: it feels the 1 to 10 N of the slide, the latch and the press. Chosen over the Nano17 because a 12 N push at the tip, 65 mm below the sensor, needs more than the Nano17's 0.5 N m torque range.

shape.note: 25 mm dia, 21.6 mm high (ATI drawing 9230-05-1312)

nano25.base_interface: 3 x M3x0.5 tapped 7.0 mm deep, equally spaced on a 20.32 mm bolt circle; 2 x 3 mm slip-fit dowel holes 7.0 deep on the same circle (mounting side)
nano25.tool_interface: 3 x M3x0.5 tapped on a 20.32 mm bolt circle + 2 x 3 mm slip-fit dowel holes 3.3 deep (tool side)
nano25.bolts: M3; do not exceed the tapped depths
nano25.cable_power: Radial cable exit on mounting side ~48 deg from the +X axis; 5.3 mm cable, strain relief; connector is 17 mm dia x 67.5 mm long; goes to NetBox/DAQ (not the Meca tool port)
nano25.notes: SI-125-3: Fxy 125 N, Fz 500 N, Txy 3 N m, Tz 3 N m; resolution 0.021 N, 0.0004 N m; single-axis overload Fxy 2300 N, Fz 7300 N, Txy 43 N m. Quote only (ATI page read 2026-10-13). Calibration SI-125-3 (125 N / 500 N / 3 N m, resolution 1/48 N and 1/1320 N m); SI-62.5-1.5 was a mistaken label corrected 2026-10-14.

adapter_plate_meca_nano25.name: Adapter plate, Meca500 to Nano25 (ours)
adapter_plate_meca_nano25.what_it_is: Our round plate that carries the Nano25 sensor on the Meca500 flange.

shape.note: 28 mm round so the Nano25's 20.32 mm bolt circle fits with its M3 heads

adapter_plate_meca_nano25.base_interface: 4 x M3 clearance on 15.5 mm PCD + 2 x 3 mm dowel pins on 15.5 mm PCD; boss into 9 H7 bore optional
adapter_plate_meca_nano25.tool_interface: 3 x M3 clearance, counterbored, + 2 x 3 mm dowels on a 20.32 mm bolt circle (Nano25 mounting side, 7 mm deep tapped holes)
adapter_plate_meca_nano25.bolts: 4 x M3 flat head (max 4 mm into the flange) + 3 x M3 socket head into the sensor
adapter_plate_meca_nano25.notes: Use only screws short enough: M3 engagement 4 mm max. Never exceed the 3.5 mm M2 depth in the sensor. Orient dowels to keep the Nano17 cable exit clear of joint 5.

servo_tool_v1.name: Servo tool v1 (ours): XL330 lead-screw gripper with three bar load cells
servo_tool_v1.what_it_is: Our own end effector: one Dynamixel XL330-M077-T lying flat in a printed body drives an M4 x 1 mm lead screw (McMaster 90500A160, PEEK anti-backlash nut 90500A310) through a 3 mm GT2 belt over the top; the nut carries the upper jaw carrier and a printed rocker couples the lower one, so both move 1.5 mm in the printed slot. Three TAL220B 5 kg bar load cells: two in series between the standoff and the body (insertion axis and vertical axis) and one as the upper finger's cross member (the pinch). Read at 1 kHz by two Adafruit ADS122C04 boards on a QT Py RP2040; one 4-core cable (24 V pair + USB data pair) along the arm. Replaces the bought gripper and the six-axis sensor.

shape.note: printed PAHT-CF shell 55 + 6 mm jaw guide, 22 across, 26 along the stroke; servo pocket open at the back

servo_tool_v1.base_interface: back end face: 4 x M3 to our bracket leg
servo_tool_v1.tool_interface: two jaws on the end face, each with M4 + 2 x 1.5 mm pins for the printed fingers (same as the MEGP pattern)
servo_tool_v1.cable_power: 5 V from a buck converter on the tool fed by a 12 V pair; Dynamixel TTL to the tool MCU; USB from the MCU to the PC
servo_tool_v1.notes: Design, not yet built. Jaw repeatability and force per step to be measured on the bench. 0.24 um per encoder step on the 1 mm lead, pinch closed on the load cells, self-locking screw holds the cable unpowered.

servo_jaw_l.name: Servo tool upper jaw carrier (printed, 16 x 14 x 4)
servo_jaw_l.what_it_is: Holds the PEEK nut on the screw (which guides it); runs in the printed slot; its exposed top face carries the upper finger (cell P's fixed end). 1.5 mm stroke.

servo_jaw_r.name: Servo tool lower jaw carrier (printed, 16 x 14 x 4)
servo_jaw_r.what_it_is: Screw clearance hole; guided by the slot and moved the opposite way by the rocker; its exposed bottom face carries the lower finger (MEGP pattern). 1.5 mm stroke.

bracket_servo.name: Cell bridge for the servo tool (ours): two bar load cells in an L, with 6061 joining plates
bracket_servo.what_it_is: Replaces the 90 degree bracket. Bar A (TAL220B 5 kg, 55 x 12.7 x 12.7) bolts under the standoff and runs east; bar B hangs off A's free end and runs along the body axis beside the body's east face. A 4 mm 6061 corner plate joins them on top; a tab and a 4 mm side plate down the body's east face carry the body (4 x M3). A reads the insertion axis, B the vertical axis.
bracket_servo.notes: cells 24 g each (upper bound), plates about 20 g; tool compliance about 0.1 mm at 12 N through the cells (bench item)

adapter_plate_meca_servo.notes: Use only screws short enough: M3 engagement 4 mm max. Never exceed the 3.5 mm M2 depth in the sensor. Orient dowels to keep the Nano17 cable exit clear of joint 5.

xl330_m077.name: Dynamixel XL330-M077-T
xl330_m077.what_it_is: The jaw servo: 5 V, 0.215 N m stall at 1.47 A, 383 rpm no load, 18 g, 20 x 34 x 26 mm, 4096 steps per turn, current-based position mode, TTL half-duplex bus.
xl330_m077.notes: Sold out at ROBOTIS America on 2026-10-13, about 2 months; order first. On the 1 mm lead: 6.4 mm/s, 0.24 um per step, about 400 N at stall (never used: the 5 N pinch is 1 percent of it).

lead_screw_m4x1.what_it_is: The jaw drive screw, coupled to the servo horn.
lead_screw_m4x1.notes: price and stock need a browser session (ESTIMATE $12)

nut_peek_m4x1.name: PEEK anti-backlash nut M4 x 1 mm (wear-compensating O-ring)

load_cell_tal220b.name: Bar load cell 5 kg TAL220B (x3)
load_cell_tal220b.what_it_is: Two at the wrist (insertion and vertical axes), one in the upper finger (pinch). 1.0 mV/V, 55 x 12.7 x 12.7 mm, safe overload 120 percent (59 N).
load_cell_tal220b.notes: in stock 2026-10-13; 24 g is a solid-block upper bound, weigh one

adc_ads122c04.name: 24-bit ADC board ADS122C04 (x2)
adc_ads122c04.what_it_is: Two differential channels each at 1 kSPS (2 kSPS turbo), I2C; about 0.07 N peak to peak on a 5 kg cell. Two boards read the three cells.

mcu_qtpy_rp2040.name: Tool microcontroller QT Py RP2040
mcu_qtpy_rp2040.what_it_is: Reads the ADCs at 1 kHz, closes the pinch loop, talks Dynamixel TTL to the servo, streams forces and position to the PC over USB full speed.

buck_d36v28f5.name: Step-down regulator 5 V 3.2 A D36V28F5
buck_d36v28f5.what_it_is: 24 V from the arm or the bench supply to 5 V for the servo and the boards.

tool_cable_cf211.name: Tool cable igus chainflex CF211-02-02-02 (2 shielded pairs, 6.5 mm OD, 51 g/m)
tool_cable_cf211.what_it_is: One cable along the arm: 24 V pair and USB data pair. 3 m.
tool_cable_cf211.notes: $4.22 per foot; USB full speed over the pair is a bench item, RS-485 is the fallback on the same board

servo_rocker.name: Servo tool rocker (printed, 3 x 3 x 22, with a 2 mm steel pivot pin)
servo_rocker.what_it_is: A lever pivoted at its centre in the end block at the carriers' front-west corner; its ends ride in a notch in each carrier: when the upper carrier moves down 1.5 mm the lower moves up 1.5 mm.
servo_rocker.notes: backlash at the lower jaw is a bench item (target under 0.05 mm)

gt2_12t_pulleys_belt.name: GT2 drive: two 12-tooth pulleys (one 4 mm bore, one on the horn pattern) and a 3 mm wide closed belt
gt2_12t_pulleys_belt.what_it_is: Links the servo's horn to the top of the lead screw 1:1 over the body, under a printed cover.
